parsed.stack: React Native, iOS + Android. Cloud vision (mid-tier model, multi-object per photo) rather than on-device, because a cluttered box needs better segmentation than a small model gives; frontier text at $0.10/M for the sell/donate/curb split. Resale comps via eBay Browse API plus a paid comps source; donation/disposal sites from a geocoded local directory. Web checkout through an external link at 0% commission, hybrid subscription plus credits for heavy weeks.
milestones: Week 1-2: one-photo-per-box capture with fast repeat shooting - an executor will take 200 of these, so the loop must be under 5 seconds a box.
Week 3-4: item detection and the three-way split, with a visible 'unsure, ask a human' bucket instead of a confident wrong call on the one valuable thing.
Week 5-6: local resale price estimates from sold comps, plus nearest donation/disposal points by postcode.
Week 7-8: the plain list output an executor can hand to a sibling or an estate sale company, with running totals.
Week 9-10: hybrid pricing, external checkout, and a pilot with two estate clearance firms and one probate solicitor as referral channel.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That sold-comp price estimates from a photo are credible enough that an executor trusts the sell/donate split - one grandmother's ring routed to 'donate' destroys trust permanently - and that the free tier is hard-capped at a few boxes, because usage is bursty (150-300 boxes in a few weeks) and an uncapped free tier turns a $4.20 payer-month into the cost of every active user.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Photograph 25 boxes from one real house clearance, run them through the vision plus comps pipeline manually, and have a working estate-clearance valuer mark the split - measure both accuracy and the metered API cost per box.
